newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - December 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - December 31.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
There will be a qualitative change in Sri Lanka's education system from tomorrow, to help the country to enter the 21st centure, says M.D.D.Peiris, Secretary Ministry of Education.
The government is in no hurry to resume negotations with the LTTE (Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam), contrary to recent speculation, government sources say.
State power monopoly Ceylon Electricity Board collects nearly 20 million rupees in fines in 1996 from power pirates, says senior board official.
Work resumed at Ceylon Steel under Korean management, after month-long protests by labour unions ended. Unions were against the sale of 90 percent of the factory to Korea Heavy in November.
Government to begin restructuring education system on January 1, in line with country's employment needs, says senior education official.
